method: Wave 3 refresh of agency-level workforce denominators for the ~42 agencies with banded consolidated_use_cases.estimated_licenses_users rows, plus OPM/Education/USAID/CFPB (flagged for special scrutiny due to major 2025 workforce disruption despite not currently having banded rows). Web research prioritizing OPM FedScope Sept/Dec 2025 snapshots (directly or via openfeds.org, a third-party FedScope aggregator, marked medium confidence), FY2026 congressional budget justifications, GAO/IG reports, and agency-official statements. ai_eligible_share/ai_eligible_rationale carried forward unchanged from Wave 1 for previously-researched agencies unless noted; originated fresh for 13 agencies with no prior wave coverage.

rows.headcount_source_title: DHS FY2026 Shutdown Contingency Plan (Procedures Relating to a Federal Lapse in Appropriations)
rows.headcount_quote: DHS estimated 249,065 of its 271,927 employees ... would be exempt and continue to work during a funding lapse.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Department total ~272k; ~60k CBP frontline + ~42k Coast Guard military + ~50k TSA screeners (all ~0.05-0.10) dominate; balanced by ~25k USCIS adjudicators, ~10k CISA, ~20k FEMA, ~20k ICE, ~15k Mgmt/HQ knowledge workers.
rows.notes: Modest net growth vs. the 260,000 Wave-1 baseline (+4.6%): CBP/ICE/Coast Guard recruiting surges partly offset CISA (-~1/3) and FEMA declines. A separate OPM FedScope civilian-cube count (via openfeds.org) shows ~227.6K, reflecting a persistent methodology gap between the DHS contingency-plan 'total employees' figure and the narrower FedScope civilian cube; 271,927 is used as the apples-to-apples comparison to the Wave-1 baseline, which used the same contingency-plan methodology.

rows.headcount_source_title: OpenFeds — Dept. of Commerce (OPM FedScope, December 2025 Employment)
rows.headcount_quote: 42.1K employees
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Carried forward from Wave 1 unchanged; workforce mix (NIST, NOAA, Census, USPTO knowledge workers vs. some field/lab staff) unlikely materially altered by RIFs.
rows.notes: -15.8% vs. 50,000 Wave-1 baseline. Corroborates a March 2025 Government Executive report of a plan to cut ~20% of Commerce staff via attrition, plus ~880 NOAA probationary layoffs (Feb 2025) and a paused ~600-notice RIF (Census/PTO/MBDA) that drew a court TRO. 42,100 is ~12-16% actual reduction so far, short of the 20% target. Source is a third-party FedScope aggregator, not a direct FedScope pull.

rows.headcount_source_title: Energy Department extends hiring freeze, deems 43% workforce non-essential in reorganization plan (Federal News Network, Apr 2025)
rows.headcount_quote: The department has nearly 16,000 employees in total ... the agency is authorized to have a workforce of more than 17,500 positions.
rows.notes: Essentially unchanged vs. 16,000 Wave-1 baseline for federal FTE, but GAO-26-108583 (Jun 2026) reports a 29.4% cumulative DOE workforce decline Dec 2024-Jan 2026 (second-steepest of 22 CFO Act agencies), implying RIF waves landed after this April 2025 snapshot and current federal headcount may be materially lower (~11k-14k) — could not obtain a clean, directly-quotable current figure, so the April 2025 snapshot is retained rather than an unverified derived number.
rows.contractor_headcount_quote: in fiscal year 2014 the agency had about 13,000 federal employees and a contractor workforce of about 94,000
rows.denominator_basis_notes: DOE's filed AI license bands appear to count site/M&O contractor staff at the national labs (Livermore, Los Alamos, Oak Ridge, PNNL, etc.), not just federal FTE, per Fable-5-team-lead direction. This 94,000 figure is the most complete DOE-wide M&O contractor total found, but it is from FY2014 (GAO-16-529) — 10+ years stale. A more current but narrower alternative is GAO-24-106861 (2024, FY2022 data): NNSA-only M&O contractors ~55,000 (excludes Office of Science labs). Flagged for a dedicated follow-up to find a current DOE-wide M&O contractor total; use with caution.

rows.headcount_source_title: CRS Report R48596, Department of Transportation Funding: FY2021-FY2025 Enacted and FY2026 Requested (July 2025), Table 2
rows.headcount_quote: The FY2026 budget request would increase DOT FTE staff by about 900, from 54,100 in FY2025 to 55,000 in FY2026.
rows.notes: -1.6% vs. 55,000 Wave-1 baseline, within noise; not a material change. This is a budget-estimate FTE ceiling, not a payroll snapshot; CRS cautions it may not reflect changes since Jan 2025. ~2,700 FAA workers took deferred resignation in 2025, but FAA is also adding ~800 FTEs for air-traffic-controller hiring, likely netting close to flat.

rows.headcount_source_title: RFK Jr. defends HHS tenure, 12% proposed budget cut (Healthcare Dive, Apr 2026), reporting House Appropriations subcommittee testimony
rows.headcount_quote: Kennedy said the HHS had around 62,000 employees after the layoffs, but has hired around 10,000 more since.
rows.notes: -10% vs. 80,000 Wave-1 baseline (current ~72,000); the trough was much deeper (~62,000, -22.5%) before partial rebound. Full timeline: pre-RIF baseline ~82,000 (Mar 2025) -> Apr 1, 2025 RIF of ~10,000 + ~10,000 more via DRP/attrition -> post-RIF trough ~62,000 by mid-2025 (some CDC/FDA reinstatements amid litigation) -> rehired back to ~72,000 by Apr 2026, with further hiring in progress. Traces to Secretary Kennedy's own testimony as reported by trade press, not an OPM FedScope or HHS FY2026 CBJ line item; still issuing new RIF notices as of May 2026 for staff 'missed' in the original round.

rows.headcount_source_title: OpenFeds — Dept. of the Treasury (OPM FedScope, December 2025 Employment)
rows.headcount_quote: Department of Treasury — 89.9K Employees ... 2025 Separations: 28.9K (+204.2% vs 2024) ... Workforce Reduction: 32.1% of workforce separated.
rows.notes: -10.1% vs. 100,000 Wave-1 baseline. Corroborated by TIGTA 'Snapshot Report: Status of the IRS's Workforce as of January 2026'; IRS (Treasury's largest bureau) fell from ~103,000 (Jan 2025) to ~74-76,000 by early/mid-2026, a well-corroborated ~27-28% cut. The magnitude doesn't fully reconcile with Treasury's overall -10% (IRS is ~80-90% of Treasury); possible explanations include filing-season staffing swings or baseline counting differences — flagged for follow-up.

rows.headcount_source_title: USDA OIG Report 25-064-01 (Dec 17, 2025)
rows.headcount_quote: As of January 11, 2025, USDA had 110,384 employees ... 20,306 employees attritted between January 12, 2025, and June 14, 2025
rows.notes: -10% vs. 100,000 Wave-1 baseline as of this OIG-anchored figure (110,384 minus 20,306 documented attrition = 90,078 as of June 2025); one of the largest 2025 RIF/DRP impacts among civilian agencies (Forest Service lost 5,860 of 35,550, 16%; Rural Development lost 36%). Further declines were reported through late 2025 via a third-party FedScope aggregator (openfeds.org), landing near ~72,000 by Dec 2025 (medium confidence, not used here in favor of the more rigorously sourced OIG figure) — flagged for a follow-up refresh.

rows.headcount_source_title: OpenFeds (OPM FedScope, Dec 2025 Employment), corroborated by VA Workforce Dashboard Issue Thirty-One (Nov 30, 2025)
rows.headcount_quote: 451.1K employees. [VA Workforce Dashboard corroboration:] Total VA Onboard = 439,822 as of 10/31/2025, explicitly excluding 'about 10,000 intermittent, non-pay, and medical resident and trainee employees.'
rows.notes: -6.4% vs. 482,000 Wave-1 baseline. VA originally announced a plan to cut up to 83,000 (Mar 2025), then walked it back to ~30,000 via attrition only with no mass RIF (Govexec, July 2025). Reduction has come almost entirely via attrition, far short of the original target.

rows.headcount_source_title: EPA Staffing Fact Sheet — Environmental Protection Network (citing EPA internal staffing plan sent to OMB, obtained via FOIA)
rows.headcount_quote: As of September 2025, EPA had 12,198 staff... 25% (about 4,000 staff) below Pre-Trump levels (16,155).
rows.notes: -24% vs. 16,000 Wave-1 baseline. Office of Research and Development eliminated July 2025; EJ/DEI offices RIF'd. EPA's own July 2025 release confirmed 3,707 terminated of 16,155 baseline via RIF + Fork-in-the-Road/DRP/VERA. Separate reporting (GovExec, Sept 2025) projected EPA heading toward ~9,700 by early 2026 — treat 12,198 as a September 2025 snapshot, likely to decline further, not a floor.

rows.headcount_source_title: NLIHC — HUD Workforce Drops by Estimated 23% Since January
rows.headcount_quote: At the beginning of the year, HUD employed around 10,000 people... an estimated 2,300 HUD staff - around 23% of HUD's workforce - have either retired, been placed on administrative leave, or accepted [DRP].
rows.notes: This is a computed figure (10,000 minus 2,300), not a directly-cited point-in-time count, and appears recycled from April 2025 reporting through October. GAO-26-108583 (Jun 2026) found HUD workforce down 30.5% Dec 2024-Jan 2026, steeper than this estimate, but no absolute headcount was extractable. HUD's own FY2026 CBJ lists FTE ~8,172, a budget-ceiling assumption not an actual post-RIF count. Treat 7,700 as a rough midpoint of a plausible 6,000-8,600 range; flagged for follow-up.

rows.headcount_source_title: GSA FY 2026 Congressional Justification
rows.headcount_quote: The FY 2026 request includes a decrease in FTE from the FY 2025 Enacted, going from 5,455 to 4,195 [PBS]; 3,436 full-time equivalent (FTE) employees [FAS/ASF]; 692 [S&E]
rows.notes: -33% vs. 12,500 Wave-1 baseline; computed sum across 3 accounts (S&E 692 + PBS 4,195 + FAS 3,436), not one stated top-line figure. Later reporting (GSA OIG via GovExec, Apr 2026) says PBS alone fell further to ~3,100 by end of 2025 due to continued RIFs, so actual mid/late-2025 GSA total is likely below 8,323. TTS down 67% since Jan 2025; 18F (~90 people) eliminated entirely.

rows.headcount_source_title: SBA FY 2026 Congressional Budget Justification and Annual Performance Plan
rows.headcount_quote: Total 6,372 [FY2024 Actual] 6,143 [FY2025 Enacted] 3,600 [FY2026 Request] (2,543) [FY2026 Incr/Decr from FY2025 Enacted]
rows.notes: -40% vs. 6,000 Wave-1 baseline. Matches independent reporting of ~43% workforce cuts under Administrator Kelly Loeffler (Federal News Network/PBS, March 2025). A Sept 29, 2025 RIF notice was briefly rescinded then reinstated (Nov 2025); some volatility around the exact final cohort is possible, but 3,600 is the best-documented current target.

rows.headcount_source_title: One Fifth of NASA's Workforce Take Voluntary Departure Options (SpacePolicyOnline.com, July 26, 2025)
rows.headcount_quote: NASA's expected remaining civil servant workforce following both DRP programs, as well as normal attrition (about 500) over the same time period: about 14,000.
rows.notes: -22% vs. 18,000 Wave-1 baseline (true pre-RIF figure was 17,391, close to but not identical to the Wave-1 baseline). Two DRP rounds + VERA/VSIP + ~500 attrition; corroborated by GovExec (Dec 2025): NASA shed ~4,000 employees, ~20% of workforce. NASA's FY2026 budget projects a further drop to 11,853 if involuntary RIFs proceed (a forward projection, not confirmed). JPL (a Caltech-operated FFRDC, ~4,500-6,000 staff) is NOT counted in NASA's civil-servant headcount under standard FedScope/OPM treatment and no evidence was found of NASA AI-tool-license figures including JPL staff — no contractor_headcount addition made for NASA, unlike DOE.

rows.headcount_source_title: TVA Form 10-K, FY ended September 30, 2025 (filed 2025-11-13), Human Capital Management
rows.headcount_quote: Employee Demographics At September 30, 2025, 2024: Number of employees 10,635, 11,312
rows.notes: Direct primary-source figure from TVA's own audited 10-K. TVA (a government corporation, not Title 5 civil service) was not subject to OPM-administered DRP/VERA/VSIP; the modest decline (11,312 to 10,635, ~6%) is not attributed to any named RIF. Flag: TVA's own 10-K shows FY2024 at 11,312, not the Wave-1 baseline of 10,000 -- the Wave-1 baseline appears to have been slightly understated. TVA separately reports ~18,000 contractors (up from 16,800); not added as contractor_headcount here since no evidence found that TVA's AI license bands include contractor staff (unlike DOE).

rows.headcount_source_title: OPM on track to eliminate 1,000 positions by the end of the year (Federal News Network, July 21, 2025)
rows.headcount_quote: OPM's workforce decreased from 3,110 employees down to about 2,000 employees since President Donald Trump took office.
rows.notes: CORRECTION: the Wave-1 baseline of 5,600 was wrong even before 2025 RIFs -- OPM's actual FedScope-era headcount (Sept 2024) was ~3,011 per USAFacts, not 5,600. On top of that, OPM underwent a ~36% RIF/VERA/VSIP reduction in 2025 (129 RIF'd, ~940 via deferred resignation/VERA/VSIP; Human Capital Data Management & Modernization office and Center for Leadership Development eliminated), landing at ~2,000. OPM's own FY2026 CBJ budgets 2,062.7 total FTE, corroborating. Do not use 5,600 going forward -- it does not match any OPM-specific source found.

rows.headcount_source_title: Federal workforce shrank 10% in Trump's first year back in office (Pew Research Center, March 13, 2026), analysis of OPM administrative data
rows.headcount_quote: The Education Department's staff shrank 42.6% between December 2024 and December 2025, from nearly 4,300 employees to fewer than 2,500. [table: 4,273 -> 2,453]
rows.notes: -44% vs. 4,400 Wave-1 baseline. Corroborated by ED's own press release (4,133 pre-RIF Jan 2025 -> ~2,183 post March 11, 2025 RIF of 1,300 layoffs + ~600 buyouts + ~100 probationary firings) and K12 Dive. A second Oct 2025 RIF (466 more) was largely rescinded by Jan 2026, stabilizing near 2,453. Department still legally exists as of mid-2026 -- no congressional authorization for closure has occurred; administration is pursuing 'shrink and transfer' (HQ consolidation, quietly moving program administration to other agencies) while FY2026 appropriations explicitly bar further relocation/reorganization without Congress. Remaining staff skew toward wind-down/administrative/legal functions given eliminated program offices, but ai_eligible_share carried forward unchanged since remaining roles are still desk-based knowledge work.

rows.headcount_source_title: From USAID to DHR: Restructuring of the American Humanitarian Engagement (Casimir Pulaski Foundation)
rows.headcount_quote: Staffing has been cut by approximately 80%, from over 1,000 to a planned 232 DHR employees, including: 113 civil service officers, 79 foreign service officers, and 40 contract specialists.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Carried forward from Wave 1 unchanged; remaining staff (civil/foreign service officers, contract specialists) are still desk-based knowledge workers, so the prior rubric-derived share is not contradicted by the workforce-composition shift, only the scale.
rows.notes: USAID NO LONGER EXISTS AS AN INDEPENDENT AGENCY. Rubio/State announced cessation of independent USAID operations effective July 1, 2025; formal RIFs completed July 1 and Sept 2, 2025. Functions absorbed into State Dept, first via an interim ~718-person transition arrangement (mid-2025), then consolidated into the new State Dept 'Bureau of Disaster and Humanitarian Response' (DHR), stood up March 20, 2026, planned at 232 staff. This row represents the DHR successor bureau, not independent USAID -- flagging for the dataset maintainer to decide whether the 'usaid' slug should be retained, retired, or re-pointed to a 'state-dhr' bureau slug in a future hierarchy update. -97.7% vs. 10,000 Wave-1 baseline either way.

rows.headcount_source_title: CFPB Workforce Restructuring Plan (Consumer Finance Monitor, citing CFPB's March 31, 2026 court filing in NTEU v. Vought)
rows.headcount_quote: By virtue of attrition, the table indicates that the headcount now is 1,174. [contrasted with] FY 2025, which was 1,723.
rows.notes: -31% vs. 1,700 Wave-1 baseline. Litigation timeline: initial mass-RIF attempt (Feb-Apr 2025, ~1,400 notices) blocked by preliminary injunction (Mar 2025); D.C. Circuit panel vacated that injunction Aug 15, 2025, allowing layoffs; D.C. Circuit granted en banc rehearing Dec 17, 2025, reinstating the injunction as of this Apr 2026 report. CFPB's March 2026 motion proposes cutting further to 556 (~68% below baseline) -- NOT yet in effect, pending litigation. 1,174 (current onboard via attrition, not the blocked RIF) is the most defensible current figure; a further cut to 556 is a likely near-future value if the injunction is lifted.

rows.headcount_source_title: SEC FY 2026 Congressional Budget Justification, corroborated by SEC Chairman Atkins's May 2025 town hall
rows.headcount_quote: at its height last year, the SEC had a total of 5,000 employees and 2,000 contractors, and that today it is down to approximately 4,200 employees and 1,700 contractors
rows.notes: -8.7% vs. 4,600 Wave-1 baseline, just under the 10% material-change threshold but part of a well-documented ongoing 2025 downsizing. FY2025 enacted FTE ceiling was 4,548; FY2026 request 4,101; GAO-26-107813 reports ~18% of SEC staff departed FY2025 via buyout/deferred-resignation (no RIF).

rows.headcount_source_title: FDIC staff reductions raise watchdog concerns (American Banker)
rows.headcount_quote: The total workforce, which was more than 6,300 employees at the end of 2024, fell to just over 5,000 by Jan. 1, 2026
rows.notes: -20.6% vs. 6,300 Wave-1 baseline. Corroborated by FDIC's 2026 Operating Budget board memo: 2026 authorized staffing (ex-OIG) is 5,386 positions, '1,337 fewer than initially approved as part of the 2025 budget,' following a 2025 Workforce Optimization Initiative.

rows.headcount_source_title: Note about the implementation of the Board's 2025 budget (Federal Reserve Board of Governors)
rows.headcount_quote: For 2025, budgeted FTE is expected to grow by 93, or 2.9 percent, over the 2024 forecast. [Table A2.6: 2024 Budget 3,148 FTE; 2025 Budget 3,291 FTE.]
rows.notes: +9.7% vs. 3,000 Wave-1 baseline, just under the material-change threshold. SCOPE CAVEAT: this is the DC Board of Governors ONLY, not the full Federal Reserve System (Board + 12 Reserve Banks + FRIT), separately budgeted at 21,411 FTE for 2025 -- do not conflate. The Fed System announced a plan in 2025 to cut headcount ~10% over the next few years via voluntary deferred resignation, so this may be a local peak before FY2026 declines.

rows.headcount_source_title: FTC FY 2026 Congressional Budget Justification
rows.headcount_quote: FY 2025 Enacted: 1,183 FTE
rows.notes: -1.4% vs. 1,200 Wave-1 baseline, not material. FY2026 request proposed a cut to 1,100 FTE, but the FY2027 CBJ separately requests 1,183 (same as FY2025 enacted), suggesting the proposed cut did not fully materialize.

rows.headcount_source_title: FCC FY 2026 Budget Estimate to Congress
rows.headcount_quote: The FCC requested 1,404 Full Time Equivalents (FTEs) for FY2026, which is a decrease of 74 FTEs compared to the FY2025 proposal
rows.notes: -6.4% vs. 1,500 Wave-1 baseline, not material. Could not independently confirm an 'actual' FY2025 enacted figure separate from the budget-request framing (PDF extraction repeatedly failed); the FY2025 proposal-level figure implies ~1,478.

rows.headcount_source_title: FERC Careers page
rows.headcount_quote: FERC has approximately 1500 employees working for the Commission's Washington, D.C. headquarters and Regional Offices in Atlanta, Chicago, New York, Portland, and San Francisco.
rows.notes: No material change vs. 1,500 Wave-1 baseline; reconfirmed with a fresh, current-dated citation. Could not access FERC's FY2025/FY2026 CBJ PDFs directly (blocked/timed out); no 2025 staffing-cut reporting found for FERC comparable to other regulators in this wave.

rows.headcount_source_title: DOL FY 2026 Congressional Budget Justification, Vol. 2, PBGC section
rows.headcount_quote: FY 2024 reflects actual FTE, with authorized FTE for FY 2024 being 970.
rows.notes: -3% vs. 1,000 Wave-1 baseline; this refines the round-number baseline to a precise stated FTE from the same FY2024 vintage rather than reflecting new 2025 data -- no FY2025/FY2026 actual figure was found (direct PDF fetch blocked on dol.gov/pbgc.gov; recovered via search-index text extraction).

rows.headcount_source_title: USITC FY 2026 Congressional Budget Justification
rows.headcount_quote: The USITC's FY 2025 staffing goal is to have an average staffing level (i.e., full-time equivalents, or FTE) of 437. As of mid-January 2025, the onboard staffing level is 430, with vacancy rates as high as 17 percent in offices responsible for statutory workload.
rows.notes: +7.5% vs. 400 Wave-1 baseline, not material. A more recent FY2025 Agency Financial Report (Dec 2025) likely has the FY-end actual figure but could not be accessed (403).

rows.headcount_source_title: DOI FY 2025 Budget Justification, National Indian Gaming Commission section
rows.headcount_quote: The Agency's actual full-time equivalents (FTE) count was 121 in FY 2023 and projected to be 140 at the end of FY 2024 and FY 2025.
rows.notes: +7.7% vs. 130 Wave-1 baseline, not material; framed by NIGC as intentional post-pandemic backfill/growth, not a cut. NIGC's FY2026 Budget Justification dropped the staffing/FTE table entirely, so this FY2025 estimate is the most current authoritative figure available.

rows.headcount_source_title: Morris K. Udall and Stewart L. Udall Foundation, FY 2026 Plan for Agency Operations in the Absence of Appropriations
rows.headcount_quote: Number of employees on board before the shutdown: As of September 30, 2025, there are 24 FTE.
rows.notes: -4% vs. 25 Wave-1 baseline, not material; refines the figure via an official OMB-required lapse-plan filing. 23 of the 24 would be furloughed in a lapse; 1 (Executive Director) retained.

rows.headcount_source_title: U.S. AbilityOne Commission FY 2026 Congressional Budget Justification (signed 2025-05-30)
rows.headcount_quote: The Commission staff (29 FTEs projected as of October 1, 2025) maintains agency operations... The Commission also has an OIG (currently 8 FTEs).
rows.notes: +5.7% vs. 35 Wave-1 baseline (not material), using the combined agency-staff (29) plus OIG (8) = 37 total, since it's unclear whether the Wave-1 baseline of 35 was agency-only or combined; flagged for scope confirmation before treating any future change as material.

rows.headcount_source_title: CSOSA Community Supervision Program (CSP) FY2025 CBJ; Pretrial Services Agency for DC (PSA) FY2025 CBJ
rows.headcount_quote: CSP: FY 2025 Base [Budgeted FTE] 725; PSA: PSA's FY 2025 President's Budget (PB) request includes ... 371 FTE
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: CSOSA's two components (725 FTE Community Supervision Program doing offender home visits/drug testing/field supervision, 371 FTE Pretrial Services doing risk-assessment interviews and lab-based drug testing) are majority field/hands-on work not easily AI-augmented, versus report-writing and case administration which are.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. CSOSA is legally split into CSP (parole/probation, 'CSOSA' proper) and PSA (a distinct entity 'within' CSOSA); total = 1,096. Neither CBJ breaks out field officers vs. pure admin HQ staff numerically.

rows.headcount_source_title: U.S. Election Assistance Commission FY2026 Congressional Budget Justification
rows.headcount_quote: FY 2024 Actual: 83 FTE ... FY 2025 Enacted: 83 FTE
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: EAC is a small, entirely desk-based policy/technical-assistance and grants agency with no field-enforcement or clinical component, though certification testing of voting-system hardware is slightly hands-on.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. FY2026 request proposes cutting to 60 FTE alongside a major budget cut (no grant funding requested); 83 is the most recent enacted/actual figure.

rows.headcount_source_title: EXIM AI Strategy for OMB Memorandum M-25-21 (v1.0, Feb 2026)
rows.headcount_quote: EXIM is an independent agency. The agency's staff numbers approximately 350 federal team members and 150 contract staff based mainly in Washington DC.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: EXIM's own AI strategy filing states staff spend the preponderance of their time in general office automation plus specialized finance/insurance applications -- an all-desk underwriter/analyst/attorney workforce with zero field component.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. FY2025 CBJ PDF returned HTTP 403 on automated fetch; relies on EXIM's own Feb 2026 AI-strategy document (an 'approximately' figure) rather than a precise budget-table FTE count.

rows.headcount_source_title: Farm Credit Administration FY2025 Proposed Budget and Performance Plan
rows.headcount_quote: Table 10. Full-time-equivalent staffing levels, FYs 2015-2025 ... 2025: 340 (authorized)
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: FCA is overwhelmingly desk-based examiners/economists/attorneys, but the core examination function requires on-site travel to Farm Credit System institutions, introducing a modest field component versus a pure-HQ regulator.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. FY2024 and FY2025 both labeled '(authorized)' rather than actuals; ~28.3% of staff projected retirement-eligible by FY2028.

rows.headcount_source_title: U.S. Federal Labor Relations Authority Congressional Budget Justification, FY2025
rows.headcount_quote: 116 full-time equivalents (FTEs) are responsible for establishing policies and guidance regarding labor-management-relations for 2.1 million non-Postal, Federal employees
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: FLRA's three components (Authority, Office of General Counsel investigators/attorneys, Office of Administrative Law Judges) are entirely desk-based legal/adjudicative professionals with no field component.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. Cut from 213 FTEs in FY2004 to 116 by FY2023; FY2025 request merely maintains that level, no growth.

rows.headcount_source_title: NCUA Board Approves 2025-2026 Budget; Succession Planning Final Rule
rows.headcount_quote: Combined, the 2025 Operating, Capital, and Share Insurance Fund administrative budgets will be $395.4 million and 1,255 staff positions.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: NCUA's workforce is dominated by credit-union examiners whose work (financial review, risk analysis, report writing) is desk/analytical despite requiring travel to credit unions.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. A 2026-2027 draft budget (Sept 2025) proposes cutting to 967 positions (-23%) following a Voluntary Separation Program (262 staff) plus hiring freeze; 1,255 is the 2025-approved level, actual current headcount trending lower toward ~967-1,200 -- flagged for follow-up.

rows.headcount_source_title: What does the National Endowment for the Arts (NEA) do? — USAFacts (sourced from OPM FedScope)
rows.headcount_quote: Some 167 of the 2.31 million total civilian federal employees work for the National Endowment for the Arts as of September 2024.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: NEA is a small grants-administration agency (grants management, panel coordination, general counsel, finance) entirely desk-based with no field component.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. No FY2025/2026 total FTE figure could be confirmed. Every NEA grant director reportedly exited in May 2025; NEA's FY2025 Agency Financial Report describes elevated 2025 attrition via DRP/VERA/VSIP under a hiring freeze. 167 is a pre-2025-disruption baseline; true current headcount is likely lower -- flagged for follow-up.

rows.headcount_source_title: National Endowment for the Humanities staff dwindles as two-thirds of workforce laid off — The Art Newspaper
rows.headcount_quote: Approximately 100 employees ... around two-thirds of the workforce, were laid off on 10 June ... Fewer than 60 employees are anticipated to remain at NEH.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Remaining NEH staff are desk-based grants/program and administrative professionals with no field component, consistent with pre-cut workforce composition.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. MAJOR 2025 DISRUPTION: pre-cut baseline was 215 (FedScope, Sept 2024) / 180 (Inside Higher Ed, April 2025). RIF effective 2025-06-10 left 'fewer than 60'; $65M cut from ~$210M budget; 1,000+ grants terminated. No more recent (late-2025/2026) confirmed figure found -- flagged for follow-up.

rows.headcount_source_title: National Transportation Safety Board FY2025 Budget Request
rows.headcount_quote: funds 455 full-time equivalent (FTE) positions [Personnel Summary table: FY2023: 409, FY2024: 418, FY2025: 455]
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Roughly half of NTSB's staff sit in modal investigative offices (Aviation, Highway, Marine, Railroad/Pipeline/Hazmat) doing field site examinations and interviews interspersed with substantial report-writing, while the rest (Safety Recommendations, R&E, ALJs, admin) is purely desk-based.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. 455 is the FY2025 requested FTE ceiling, not a census count; reporting suggests actual mid-2025 staffing trailed it (~400-445) amid deferred-resignation offers and a hiring freeze, with NTSB securing a partial exemption.

rows.headcount_source_title: U.S. Office of Special Counsel FY2025 Congressional Budget Justification
rows.headcount_quote: OSC's approved request is $33,759,000 to fund approximately 135 FTEs and related non-personnel costs for FY 2025.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OSC's workforce is almost entirely attorneys/investigators doing casework (document review, interviews, legal analysis) with no physical/site-inspection component; former field offices in Dallas/Detroit are now virtual.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. Program breakdown: Investigation & Prosecution Division 64, Operations 17, Case Review/Clerk 12, Whistleblower Disclosure Unit 10, Hatch Act Unit 8, plus smaller units.

rows.headcount_source_title: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission FY2025 Performance Budget and Justification
rows.headcount_quote: support 63 full-time equivalent (FTE) positions ... in fiscal year (FY) 2025
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OSHRC is a purely adjudicatory body (ALJs, three commissioners, general counsel, clerical staff) resolving OSHA contest cases entirely through hearings/legal review, with zero inspection function of its own (that belongs to OSHA/DOL, a separate agency).
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. Breakdown: ALJ function 27 FTE, Commission-Review Level 28 FTE (incl. 3 Commissioners), Office of Executive Director 8 FTE. Confirmed not to be confused with OSHA (the DOL enforcement agency).

rows.headcount_source_title: Surface Transportation Board FY2025 Budget Request (President's Budget Submission)
rows.headcount_quote: The Board's funding request is based on a projected staffing level of 152 FTEs.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: STB staff is organized entirely into attorneys, economists, and financial/transportation/environmental analysts plus HR/IT/paralegal support -- no field or inspection function (rail safety inspection belongs to FRA, not STB).
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. No 2025 disruption found for STB; it was not named in the March 2025 EO targeting small agencies (IMLS, Woodrow Wilson Center, FMCS, USAGM, USICH, CDFI Fund, MBDA).

rows.headcount_source_title: USTDA Congressional Budget Justification for FY2025
rows.headcount_quote: Personnel Ceiling (FTEs) 68 [FY2023 actual] 68 [FY2024 estimate] 73 [FY2025 request]
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: USTDA staff are almost entirely desk-based program/grants and technical-assistance professionals administering feasibility-study/trade-facilitation grants, with no field or frontline function.
rows.notes: First wave-3 origination for this agency; no prior baseline existed. Explicitly checked for 2025 disruption (unlike USAID/State foreign-assistance-adjacent agencies) and found NONE -- USTDA was not among agencies targeted by the March 2025 EO; FY2026 budget analysis shows funding equal to the FY25 enacted level ($87M). FY2026/FY2027 CBJs lack an FTE table, so 73 (FY2025) is the most recent sourced figure.
